A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Faster Cascades via Speculative Decoding. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original T5 translation and summarization experiments, including measured latency and quality in Section 6, Table 2, and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original T5 results and reports additional token-specific cascade, Gemma, sensitivity, and baseline-comparison experiments in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 and Algorithm 6 introduce token-specific deferral, three heuristic rules, and a target distribution that redistributes rejected draft probability mass through the verifier. This substantially extends v1's prefix-level selection between whole model distributions. Algorithm 4 also changes the extra-token distribution after all drafts are accepted from p to the target distribution pi.

E1.justification: v2 retains WMT, CNN/Daily Mail, and XSum, while adding GSM8K mathematical reasoning, MBPP programming, and SQuAD 2.0, WebQuestions, Natural Questions, and TriviaQA question answering. The Gemma experiments also introduce few-shot evaluation alongside the existing task-specific fine-tuning experiments.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated comparison with the original BiLD algorithm, including its fallback phase and deterministic rollback, alongside the retained BiLD* adaptation (Appendix E.5, Figure 8). The other baseline families remain. Tuned Lossy* is retained from v1 Appendix D.3, rather than newly introduced.

E3.justification: v2 adds T5 temperatures 0.1 and 0.5 and block sizes 3 and 7 to the earlier settings. New Gemma evaluations use 2B-to-9B/27B configurations, 1,000 prompts per dataset, few-shot prompting, and rejection-rate cost measurements with gamma=1. Appendix E.1 also changes the stated BiLD discrepancy from log probability to negative log probability, although E.5 retains the old sign; rerunning existing comparisons is not established.

E4.justification: New analyses examine temperature sensitivity, block-size sensitivity, and differences among the three token-specific rules (Appendices E.3, E.4, and E.7). Appendix E.5 tests whether BiLD* represents the original BiLD across fallback thresholds and window sizes. These substantially expand analysis beyond v1's decoding-regime comparisons and lossy-decoding tuning study.

E5.justification: Both v1 Appendix D.1 and v2 Appendix E.1 report average runtime over three trials. v2 does not introduce seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 preserves every existing numerical row and adds Token results. For WMT Small-to-Large at T=1, its best BLEU is 22.50 versus the retained OPT value 18.33, while its quality-matched speedup is 1.85x versus OPT's 1.95x. New figures report Gemma and sensitivity results. The earlier WMT Base-to-Large latency curve in v1 Figure 3 is omitted; most other earlier curves are retained or relocated.

T1.justification: The existing optimal-deferral lemmas, regret bounds, and proofs are retained. v2 adds formal token-specific target definitions and an associated constrained optimization problem with a simple special case in Appendix D, without a general optimality solution. It removes v1 Remark 3's explicit finite-temperature optimal-deferral formulation, while retaining the greedy-decoding equivalence.

C1.justification: The central claims about combining cascading with speculative execution and characterizing optimal deferral remain. v2 adds token-specific variants to the stated contributions and broadens the explicitly claimed empirical scope from T5 experiments to Gemma and tasks including reasoning, coding, and question answering.

C2.justification: v2 explains why distribution-mode confidence can accept poor sampled tokens, why token-specific advantages diminish at lower temperatures, and why OPT behaves differently with Gemma. It also explains large-block rollback costs, qualifies BiLD's target-distribution interpretation, and newly acknowledges higher total compute than sequential cascades. Calibration dependence and local-objective concerns largely develop qualifications already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds Gemma configuration details, including instruction-tuned versus pre-trained models, prompt counts, generation-length limits, and shot counts, plus original-BiLD parameter choices. Existing T5 training, hardware, and checkpoint disclosures remain. Appendix E promises code and a tutorial notebook, but does not establish an actual release. The explicit finite-temperature implementation guidance from v1 is lost.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Gemma, the new datasets, and EAGLE, and more explicitly distinguishes its quality-cost objective from state-of-the-art lossless inference acceleration. BiLD remains the closest comparator and the broader related-work organization is retained. Author-year formatting and duplicate publication/preprint entries do not constitute additional research positioning.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and much of the prose remain. v2 clarifies the motivation and evaluation scope, merges the deferral-risk and optimal-rule subsections, reorganizes experimental exposition, moves greedy-decoding discussion into the appendix, and adopts author-year citations. New scientific sections extend the existing structure rather than comprehensively rewriting it.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: Figure 2 becomes a two-panel T=0.5 comparison, earlier plots are regrouped in the appendix, and new Gemma, temperature, block-size, BiLD, and token-variant displays are added. Table 2 gains a Token row, Algorithm 6 is added, and Figure 1's axes and caption clarify the deferral-rate denominator.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support was confined to fine-tuned T5 translation/summarization and a modified BiLD comparator. v2 substantially strengthens the evidence through decoder-only Gemma experiments across reasoning, coding, and QA, comparison with original BiLD, and controlled sensitivity and variant analyses. These reveal important boundaries of OPT and support the motivation for token-specific deferral. The gains outweigh the loss of explicit finite-temperature guidance, although Gemma efficiency remains supported by rejection-rate proxies rather than measured latency and statistical reporting is unchanged.
